newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ASSA ABLOY REPEATS BRIGHT '97 FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: ASSA ABLOY REPEATS BRIGHT '97 FORECAST.

text.p: Swedish lock maker Assa Abloy on Thursday repeated its expectations of a continued good profit development for 1997 as it posted a 51 percent rise in pre-tax profit for the first six months of the year.
Assa Abloy reported a pre-tax profit of 225 million crowns and a 31 percent climb in sales to 3.04 billion crowns.
For comparable units sales rose 10 percent in the half year and and by 12 percent in the U.S..
"The expectation of a continued good profit development for Assa Abloy in 1997 expressed in the annual report remains unchanged," the company said in a statement.
Assa Abloy's share price rose on the result, rising to 180 crowns, which was two crowns above Wednesday's closing price, from trading at 177 crowns before the report.
Assa Abloy said the group's organic growth continued in the second quarter due mainly to a rise in the sales rate in the Nordic countries.

Sale at Abloy in Finland were going particularly well, rising 19 percent to 248 million crowns, with help from an increase in new construction and increasing volumes for industrial and electromechanical products.
Exports to the Baltic states and Russia continued to increase.
Sales growth of between two and eight percent was seen in the British operations, Ruko in Denmark and IKON in Germany.
Swedish units were starting to pick up despite a weak construction cycle with sales rising 12 percent to 421 million crowns in the six months to June 30, 1997.
The U.S. operations, Sargent, Curries, Arrow and others, continued to show strong growth, with sales rising 12 percent to 151 million crowns in the first half against a year ago.
Assa Abloy said the newly acauired units in France, including the Vachette group, have been consolidated and about one month's invoicing was included in six month sales.
Sales in the hotel card division, Vingcard, rose 12 percent to 314 million crowns.
